title: Motivation
text:
Motivation
RNN limitations
• Token-by-token computation limits parallel training throughput.
• Information from far positions must pass many recurrent steps.
• Optimization over long contexts is often unstable or inefficient.
CNN limitations
• Convolutions are parallel, but each layer has local receptive fields.
• Capturing long-range context requires deeper stacks or larger kernels.
• Context expansion is indirect compared with direct token-token
interaction.
Key idea
At each layer, every token can directly read from all tokens in the sequence.

title: Limitation of attention
text:
Limitation of attention
What attention cannot do
• Attention only recombines existing value vectors
• It cannot create new features beyond linear mixtures
Implication
• Representation power depends heavily on:
• value projection WV
• feed-forward network (FFN)
Takeaway
Attention selects information; FFN creates new representations.

Transformer block

Functional roles in this block
• MHA (self-attention): mixes information across token positions, so
each token can read global context.
• LayerNorm (LN): stabilizes activation scale and helps optimization in
deep stacks.
• FFN: transforms channels per token (expand →nonlinearity →project),
increasing representational capacity.
• Skip connection: preserves identity signal and improves gradient flow
through deep networks.
Reading
This block alternates token mixing (MHA) and channel mixing (FFN), with
normalization and residual paths for stable training.

x →Sublayer →+x →LayerNorm
Pre-norm (common modern style)
x →LayerNorm →Sublayer →+x
Practical note
Pre-norm is usually easier to optimize in deeper stacks; post-norm can be less
stable without careful training setup.

title: Where computation goes
text:
Where computation goes
• Q,K,V projection: O(nd2)
• Attention matrix: O(n2d)
• FFN: O(nddff ) ≈O(4nd2) when dff = 4d
Key insight
• Large n →attention dominates
• Large d or large dff →FFN/projections dominate

title: CNN vs Attention (deeper view)
text:
CNN vs Attention (deeper view)
• CNN:
• Strong inductive bias (locality, translation invariance)
• Efficient but less flexible
• Attention:
• Weak inductive bias
• Learns relationships directly from data
Trade-off
• CNN = bias + efficiency
• Attention = flexibility + data dependency

title: Minimal PyTorch attention
text:
Minimal PyTorch attention
scores = (Q @ K.transpose (-2,
-1)) / (d ** 0.5)
scores = scores + mask
A = torch.softmax(scores , dim=-1)

keras
from
keras

layers

# Self -attention
sublayer
x1 = layers. LayerNormalization ()(inp)
a = layers. MultiHeadAttention (num_heads =8, key_dim =64)(x1 , x1)
x2 = layers.Add()([inp , a])
# FFN
sublayer
x3 = layers. LayerNormalization ()(x2)
f = layers.Dense (2048 ,
activation="gelu")(x3)

title: Engineering insight
text:
Engineering insight
• Runtime cost is often dominated by attention activation tensors.
• Parameter count is often dominated by FFN projections.
• Throughput depends strongly on batch size, sequence length, and kernel
implementation.
Takeaway
For deployment, optimize sequence length and memory movement before only
scaling model width.
